headline: Ordered Hurricane Betty’s, 350 Southbridge Street, to close at 8:00 p.m. and gave Next Level Hospitality, 48 Green Street, a three-day suspension.
summary: The Commission approved 14 license and permit requests, including one-day liquor and entertainment licenses for Halloween events. It found that Next Level Hospitality, LLC, 48 Green Street, violated a rule over a promotion offering a free shot with a drink. After an October 11, 2026, shooting at Hurricane Betty’s in which one man died, community members raised public safety concerns.

Call to Order – 10:00 A.M. 
            
Minutes: October 8, 2026, October 13, 2026 
 
Upon a roll call the Commission voted 3-0 to approve the minutes of October 8, 2026, and October 
13, 2026.

Violation Hearings 
 
17. Marlboro Foods, Inc, 1442 Grafton Street 
• Violation of Rules #4, #20, #21 
        
Nakula Patel and Joshi Patel appeared upon behalf of the item.
Following the October 8, 2026 , hearing, it was determined that the Licensee has two premises. It 
was determined that at the October 8, 2026, hearing, the Commission believed there had been a 
prior violation at the 1442 Grafton Street location. This was in error, as there had not been a prior 
violation at 1442 Grafton Street location item was reheard. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to issue a warning. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated August 14, 2026.  
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to issue a warning. 
 
18. Next Level Hospitality, LLC, 48 Green Street  
Violation of Rule #14, 204 CMR 4.03 
 
Cam Brigham appeared to answer to the violation and waived his right to counsel. 
 
Sgt. Needham presented the following: 
 
On Monday, September 28, 2026, the Worcester Police Alcohol Enforcement Unit received an email from 
the City of Worcester License Commission regarding a happy hour violation at the location. Attached to the 
email was a screenshot of a promotional flyer that had been posted on Instagram. The flyer promoted "Thirsty 
Thursday, College Night," offering a free shot with the first drink at 1885, located at 48 Green Street. 
  
On October 1, 2026, Officer Glenn Stout visited the premises and requested the off-duty bartender to contact 
a member of management. Shortly after, Cameron Brigham, the manager on record, called Officer Stout. 
The officer informed him of the complaint, and Mr. Brigham stated that he had promptly removed the 
promotion from social media and would review all social posts before they were published in the future. 
 
Mr. Brigham stated that everything stated was correct. He said as soon as he saw on Instagram he deleted 
and he had talk with marketing team that prior to anything being posted has to be reviewed by him as he 
aware that alcohol cannot be given away. 
 
The Commission noted that there were previous violations on file. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3- 0 to issue a three day suspension with one day served-  
November 5, 2026. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated October 6, 2026. 
 
Status Hearing 
 
19. Jolo, Inc. dba Hurricane Betty’s, 350 Southbridge Street 
 
Attorney Sean Smith along with Scottie Foreman appeared upon behalf of item.
Attorney Smith stated that the grand jury is still investigating the case. 
 
Sgt. Needham presented the following: 
 
On October 11, 2026, Worcester Police responded to Hurricane Betty’s in response to a ShotSpotter 
activation that came in. Responding officers arrived at scene and found one adult male in the 
roadway suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. The victim was treated on scene and transported 
to UMASS hospital where he received further treatment but succumbed to his injuries. Officers were 
then notified of a second gun shot wound victim had been transported to UMASS Memorial on 
Belmont Street. It was determined through investigation that the second victim was involved in the 
incident at Hurricane Betty’s and received their wounds as result of that incident. 
 
Worcester Police began process of investigation and during the process received video evidence 
from the establishment which showed a number of violations of the Rules and Regulations of the 
Worcester License Commission. 
 
Captain James Johnson from the Worcester Police stated due to serious of the violations he would 
recommend that establishment be closed by 8:00 p.m.  
 
Several individuals from the community, including friends and family of the individual who was shot, 
expressed their deep concerns regarding the license holder's failure to address public safety issues. 
They conveyed their belief that patrons and community members are not safe and urged the 
Commission to thoroughly review the various concerns and safety matters associated with this 
location, as they seek accountability. 
 
Chair Vigliotti stated that this is a serious matter and he was on Commission when the first homicide 
occurred and now another incident does not look well on the premises. 
 
Upon a motion made and duly seconded the Commission voted 3-0 that establishment must close at 
8:00 p.m. 
 
List of Exhibits: Police report dated October 19, 2026. 
 
Other Business 
 
Daylight Savings Time-Filed 
 
Adjournment 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to adjourn the meeting at 11:07 a.m.
